text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: HIGH - inference-gateway (us-west2) 5xx error-rate spike. Service: inference-gateway-prod. Trigger: 5xx_rate > 4% for 2m. Pager: @sara (oncall) -> oncall@sre.team :pagerduty-bot: ref: PD#INC-58421

sara (oncall): Acked PD. Looking at dashboards now.

mike (sre): I see the 5xx spike aligning with a burst of long tail requests to /v1/generate, p95 token latency jumped. Could be a particular model or route.

jordan (runtime): Rolling logs show a bunch of 502s from the grpc proxy to worker-pool-3. Kernel OOM? or connection resets.

anika (eng): Any deploys in the last 30m? I don't see a recent canary.

sara (oncall): No deploys. Traffic shows a single customer route (cust-A) with lot of concurrent streams. They had a big batch job starting ~30s before spike.

leo (support): I've pinged cust-A contact and asked them to pause the job. They replied "on it" and will throttle.

mike (sre): Quick mitigation options: 1) Throttle cust-A at the ingress routing rule 2) Reroute cust-A to a lower-cost model variant (smaller memory) 3) Increase worker-pool size for pool-3 (scale up) 4) Enable temporary 503 fallback to avoid 502 cascades. Thoughts?

jordan (runtime): pool-3 nodes are at ~92% memory usage. Scaling up will take ~30s to warm; warming KV cache will add latency. Throttling cust-A is fastest.

sara (oncall): Agreed. Mike, can you apply a soft limit on the cust-A route? Something like max_concurrency=8 and slower rate-limit?

mike (sre): On it. Applying policy now:

```
# routing control
redwoodctl routes update --id cust-A --max-concurrency 8 --rate-limit 120/s --note "auto-mitigation 5xx spike"
```

mike (sre): Policy applied. Confirming route metrics...

incident-bot: action-log: route update accepted by control-plane (req_id: 0a3f9).

jordan (runtime): After policy enforcement I see immediate drop in new connections to pool-3. 5xx rate dropping from 6.1% -> 2.4% in the last 30s.

leo (support): Cust-A confirmed they paused their job.

anika (eng): Good catch. We should still patch the underlying cause. Those 502s from grpc proxy -> worker might indicate transient connection saturation. Let's keep the pool scaled a bit and investigate kernel/network errors.

mike (sre): I'll keep one extra node in pool-3 for 15m to stabilize. Command: `infractl pool scale pool-3 +1 --ttl 15m`

mike (sre): Done. Warmup starting.

jordan (runtime): Fetching worker logs for peer resets: `gcloud logging read "resource.labels.instance_id=~'worker-pool-3.*' AND severity>=ERROR" --limit 50`

jordan (runtime): Found repeated `connection reset by peer` entries around spike start, but no OOM. Looks like upstream keepalive timeouts and an overloaded accept loop. Increasing keeper threads helped previously.

anika (eng): Can we bump proxy keepalive and lower max-requests-per-conn temporarily? Makes sense to avoid long-lived stalls.

mike (sre): I'll patch the proxy config in staging and roll to canary in prod quickly.

sara (oncall): For customer-facing comms: Leo, can you mark PD incident as "mitigated - routing throttle" and email cust-A with note that we applied a temporary throttle and request their long-run job be paced?

leo (support): On it. Draft: "We observed elevated 5xxs impacting inference across us-west2 tied to a high-concurrency job. We've temporarily limited your concurrency to 8 to protect platform stability. Please resume with lower concurrency or contact us if you need reserved capacity." Sending now.

pagerduty-bot: PD note updated: status -> acknowledged, notes -> mitigation: route throttle + pool scale.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: 5xx rate trending down. Current 5xx_rate 1.1% (5m). Keep monitoring for next 10m.

jordan (runtime): Can we add a short-term rule to auto-deprioritize routes that cause >40% of 5xx volume for 1m? That could auto-protect other customers.

anika (eng): Good idea. But let's be careful with noisy neighbor false positives. Maybe combine with concurrency > 50 and sustained error share > 40% for 30s.

mike (sre): I'll open a quick RFC and prototype. For now, incremental: add an alert on error-share per-route.

sara (oncall): I'll annotate the incident timeline and mark mitigation completed at 1768888285. We'll leave follow-up action items in the ticket.

leo (support): Cust-A acknowledged and will reschedule their batch. No further customer escalations.

anika (eng): Postmortem action items I already created: 1) Add per-route error-share alert 2) Proxy keepalive tuning + config rollout 3) Investigate accept loop saturation 4) Consider per-route concurrency guards in control-plane.

mike (sre): I'll monitor for 20m and then remove the extra pool node.

incident-bot: incident closed for now (auto-archive pending). Final note: mitigation successful; root cause likely request burst from a single customer saturating proxy accept loop.

sara (oncall): Thanks all. Handing off to Mike + Anika for follow-ups. :heart:

leo (support): Adding link to PD ticket and customer convo in the incident thread: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/incidents/INC-58421

mike (sre): Last check: 5xx_rate steady at 0.9%. I'll remove TTL on the extra node in 12m if stable.

jordan (runtime): I'll queue the proxy config tweak for canary tomorrow morning and add load test to validate.

anika (eng): Thanks everyone. Closing slack thread."
